findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the `multi-project-bridge` stamp is made to track the mapping ATOMICALLY with the transition to a second project (e.g. the `bridge projects` set path re-stamps under the same store lock, or documents that a same-transaction re-stamp closes the un-stamped window) rather than relying on a later ensure sweep.
evidence: Compat gate check_store_compat runs 'inside rebar._store.lock.acquire' on every locked mutation, but write_compat_record / the re-stamp runs only via _store_compat_unit in run_ensures
run_ensures is invoked at init/boot/fsck, and the write-path only emits a best-effort pending HINT (maybe_emit_pending_hint), it does not run the sweep
Plan Compatibility: 'the ensure re-stamping on the next covered write' — but a covered write does not itself run the store-compat unit
findings.finding: The final AC requires that a multi-project store 'carries multi-project-bridge' so an older binary refuses writes, but the capability stamp is only (re)written by _store_compat_unit, which runs solely inside run_ensures (init / MCP-boot / fsck --repair) — NOT on every covered write. A `bridge projects` set that adds a second project mutates the mapping without necessarily triggering an ensure sweep, so the .store-compat.json stamp lags the mapping's multi-project state until the next sweep. During that window a store is genuinely multi-project yet un-stamped, and an older binary is not gated — the very duplication failure the Compatibility section says the stamp prevents.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (final) + 'Compatibility and rollback'; interaction of bridge projects command with _store_compat_unit / ensures.run_ensures
scenarios: Operator runs `bridge projects set` to add a second project, then an older binary performs a write before any init/boot/fsck sweep re-stamps

findings.finding: The multi-project inbound fetch child scopes JQL fan-out and the truncation ceiling per project but does not address the three per-project enrichment passes the current fetcher runs (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map), each of which takes exactly one project key; fanning out the base JQL while leaving enrichment single-project silently drops inbound parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Multi-project inbound fetch'; vs src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:593-718 (_build_snapshot enrichment)
findings.suggested_fix: Have _build_snapshot iterate the configured project set for the enrichment step too — call get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map once per project and merge each result — and add the multi-project enrichment fidelity to the two-project fetch acceptance test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add enrichment fan-out to child 1734: per-project get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map calls merged into the shared snapshot, plus an AC asserting one enrichment pass per project and both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot.
evidence: Parent AC2: 'checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot'.

Parent decomposition, Multi-project inbound fetch child: 'the three per-project enrichment passes (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map) also fan across every configured project — one call per project, results merged into the shared snapshot keyed by issue ... Enrichment fidelity joins the two-project fetch acceptance test.'

Child 1734 ACs mention only 'one JQL pair per project', 'source project and repos', 'truncation ceiling per project', 'single-project regression', 'zero-issue project' — none names get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map or merged enrichment data.
Child 1734 Approach/Scope discuss only jqls_for fan-out; no enrichment-map fan-out is described.
findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires that one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot, but child 1734 — the sibling the parent decomposition assigns this to ('Enrichment fidelity joins the two-project fetch acceptance test') — carries no acceptance criterion, approach note, or scope line covering enrichment fan-out. Its ACs cover only the JQL pair per project and the recorded project/repos. No other sibling covers per-project enrichment either.
scenarios: Two configured projects; enrichment (parent/comment/issuelink) is fetched for only the first project, silently dropping parent/comment/issuelink data for the second — exactly the failure the parent decomposition warns about ('would silently drop parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one'), and the completion verifier for AC2 has no test asserting the per-project enrichment call count or merged data.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 1734's Approach/Scope to fan get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map across every configured project (one call each per project, merged keyed by issue) and add an acceptance criterion asserting the per-project enrichment call count and both projects' enrichment data in the merged snapshot, matching parent AC2's wording.

findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion 2 requires that 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) is issued per configured project, with both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot' — but the multi-project inbound fetch child (1734) covers only the JQL-pair fan-out and source-project recording; its acceptance criteria say nothing about the three per-project enrichment passes. No sibling covers the enrichment remainder, so this half of AC2 is uncovered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion to child 1734 asserting one enrichment call per configured project for each of get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map with both projects' data merged into the snapshot, and add the enrichment merge site (fetcher._build_snapshot:577-685) to its scope; this also closes the G4 owned-by-none gap on the enrichment merge that both 1734 and a33c touch but neither owns.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign an owner for the store-compat re-stamp-on-divergence behaviour covering BOTH transitions (add multi-project-bridge at a second project AND remove it on reverse) and add an AC testing the reverse/removal transition, since 462d only tests the add direction.
evidence: Parent decomposition, Store-compat capability stamp child: 'change _store_compat_unit's check-then-act from "blob absent" to "committed required_capabilities != desired set from the mapping" (today it never re-stamps a converged store, so it could neither add the capability at a second project nor remove it on the reverse transition); ... test covers BOTH transitions.'

Child 462d AC: 'The capability is stamped only when the mapping holds more than one project; checked by a paired test over a one-project and a two-project mapping.' — this is the ADD/one-vs-two contrast, not a remove-on-reverse-transition test.
Child 67f9 ACs cover KNOWN_CAPABILITIES registration and fail-closed read/write-gate only; no stamping or reverse transition.

Roster contains no child titled or scoped as the standalone store-compat stamp with re-stamp-on-divergence logic; the parent's decomposition line has no corresponding roster entry beyond 462d (add-only) and 67f9 (register-only).
findings.finding: The parent decomposition names a distinct 'Store-compat capability stamp' child whose defining behaviour is changing _store_compat_unit's check-then-act to re-stamp on divergence so it can BOTH add multi-project-bridge at a second project AND remove it on the reverse transition, 'test covers BOTH transitions.' No sibling in the roster owns the reverse (removal) transition. Child 462d only stamps (adds) the capability when the mapping holds more than one project; it never tests removal when a store drops back to one project. Child 67f9 only registers the capability name and tests fail-closed reads, not stamping. The reverse-transition behaviour is owned by NO sibling.
scenarios: A store that was multi-project reverts to a single project; the ensure unit never removes the multi-project-bridge capability from required_capabilities, so the store remains permanently fail-closed to older binaries even though the compatibility hazard is gone — the reverse-transition behaviour the parent decomposition calls out is delivered by no child.
AC7's 'single-project store remains writable' is satisfied for a never-multi store, but a demoted store is not returned to writable-by-old-binary, and no test asserts the removal transition.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend child 462d's stamp unit to compute required_capabilities from the mapping on every sweep (re-stamp when committed set != desired, covering removal) with a paired both-transitions AC, or add the missing standalone 'Store-compat capability stamp' child named in the parent decomposition with that behaviour and test.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The 'Ticket repos field' child (schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping) has no covering acceptance criterion — no AC verifies the repos field is written or defaulted from the mapping.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Ticket repos field'; Acceptance Criteria

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting an attempt to change the project of an already-bound ticket is rejected (promote-only).
evidence: Child text: 'promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket)'.
The empty-project criterion (AC3) covers only that an explicitly-empty ticket produces no mutation; no criterion asserts that changing the project of an already-bound ticket is rejected.
findings.finding: The 'promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket)' described in the Ticket project field child has no covering acceptance criterion.
scenarios: Executor implements the promote-only guard but no test asserts a bound ticket's project change is refused; the guard could regress silently.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC2 (or add a criterion) to assert the truncation ceiling is applied per configured project rather than shared across the fan-out.
evidence: Child text: 'per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project'.
AC2 asserts one JQL pair and one enrichment pass per project and merged snapshot fidelity, but does not assert per-project truncation-ceiling scoping.

scenarios: A shared (rather than per-project) truncation ceiling ships and one busy project starves others of results without any test catching it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the mapping-seed ensure unit BEFORE `store-compat` in `REGISTRY_IDS` (or make `_store_compat_unit` read the committed-tree mapping, not the just-seeded worktree) so the capability stamp is computed against a converged mapping within a single `run_ensures` sweep.
evidence: REGISTRY_IDS = (env-id, gc-config, merge-ours, gitattributes, gitignore, store-compat) — store-compat is last
run_ensures iterates 'for uid in REGISTRY_IDS' in order under a single write_lock
Plan: "'committed required_capabilities' != desired set from the mapping" — the unit now depends on the mapping's committed state
The mapping-seed 'ensure unit' is a separate new unit whose position vs store-compat is unspecified
findings.finding: The plan changes _store_compat_unit to compute the desired capability set 'from the mapping', and adds a new mapping-seed ensure unit, but does not pin their relative order in REGISTRY_IDS. store-compat is currently ordered LAST in REGISTRY_IDS and run_ensures iterates that tuple in order under one lock; if store-compat evaluates before the mapping seed has written/converged projects.json on a fresh sweep, it stamps required_capabilities against an absent/unseeded mapping and mis-computes the capability set.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Store-compat capability stamp'; src/rebar/_store/ensures.py REGISTRY_IDS; src/rebar/_commands/init.py:509 _store_compat_unit
scenarios: A single-pass ensure sweep on a store being converted to multi-project where the seed unit and the stamp unit run in one run_ensures call
First MCP-boot / fsck --repair sweep on a store whose mapping was just written
findings.suggested_fix: State in the 'Store-compat capability stamp' and 'Project mapping store' children that the mapping-seed unit id is inserted into REGISTRY_IDS ahead of 'store-compat', and that _store_compat_unit derives its desired capability set from the committed tickets-branch mapping blob.

findings.finding: The 'Ticket repos field' child (schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping) has no covering acceptance criterion — no AC asserts the repos field is written, read, or defaulted from the mapping.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Ticket repos field'; Acceptance Criteria
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'An ingested ticket records the repo set derived from its project's mapping entry; checked by a reconciler test asserting the repos field on a created ticket matches the mapping.'

findings.finding: The promote-only rule ('cannot change project of a bound ticket') under the Ticket project field child has no covering acceptance criterion, so the invariant is described but never verified.

The 'Ticket repos field' child delivers substantive functional work — schema, reducer, create-time arg, and inbound defaulting of repos from the mapping — but no acceptance criterion covers it. The 'two new ticket fields' are in Scope, yet only the project field is verified (AC3 empty-project, AC4 explicit-project); the repos field and its mapping-driven inbound defaulting have no covering criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria / Child decomposition — 'Ticket repos field'
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'An inbound ticket with no explicit repos records the repos derived from the store mapping for its project; checked by a reconciler test asserting the recorded repos on an ingested ticket match the mapping entry.'

findings.finding: The store-compat 'conditional capability stamp' child does not address that the existing store-compat ensure unit only writes the record when the committed blob is ABSENT (tree-check -> ok) and never re-stamps a converged store, nor that KNOWN_CAPABILITIES is currently empty; as written the mechanism cannot add multi-project-bridge when a store gains a second project after the record already exists, nor remove it on the reverse transition, and a binary writing the capability would fail its own gate.
findings.location: Scope: src/rebar/_store/compat.py — the conditional capability stamp; child 'Store-compat capability stamp'; AC line 7
findings.suggested_fix: Change _store_compat_unit's check-then-act from 'blob absent' to 'committed required_capabilities != desired set computed from the mapping', add `multi-project-bridge` to KNOWN_CAPABILITIES, and have write_compat_record accept/compute the capability list; cover both the add (>1 project) and remove (back to <=1) transitions in the store-compat test.
